decisions.D8: The runtime exposes a finite set of well-defined operations bounded by what the evaluation needs; everything else is refused.
decisions.D9: LLM calls are a hook point only: the hook asks policy before the call; content sent to or returned by the model is not guaranteed.
decisions.D10: This catalog covers the pandas application only.
decisions.D11: Application graph code and the framework are trusted; only tool implementations and generated code are contained.

citation_format: <path under source_root>::<Qualified.name>; request_classes name classes in security/objects.py; router_methods name methods of security/host_router.py HostRouter; refusal kind registered means a key of security/unsupported.py REGISTRY or a code starting with a PREFIXES key, kind literal means a string constant in the cited source file

operations.purpose: Run model-generated Python over the granted dataframe inside the isolated Linux worker and return inert JSON.
operations.trust_note: Generated code is untrusted (D11). It runs only in the bubblewrap worker with the granted authority; the lifecycle is checked by the Lean receipt checker before GO and before result release.

request_shape.input: one ToolCall to the single `compute` tool with args {code, function_name, data (JSON of DataFrame.to_dict), memory_limit_mb, data_format, sandbox_serialization, computation_api} (eval/apps/pandas/integration.py bridge; codec eval/apps/pandas/sandbox_codec.py)
request_shape.output: security/execution.py::HostExecutionResult carrying {result, error} JSON; result is decoded by the recursive-json-v2 codec, never executed

operations.policy_hook: HostRouter.invoke: policy tool permission and DAC/MAC grant, then EnforcementCoordinator obligation negotiation (lean_grant bounded native grant) before the worker is activated
operations.effect: One sandboxed process: read access to the granted dataset bytes only, no network, no process creation, rlimits, seccomp, Landlock; confirmed cleanup; returns a HostExecutionResult

proof.note: Premises of linux-worker-compute (OS, bubblewrap, interpreter, policy authorization) remain premises.

operations.purpose: Release the final answer (table, plot, routing, state) to a destination with an exact label and clearance check.
operations.trust_note: Model-influenced content leaves only through OutputMediator; the caller gets exactly the authorized content within clearance.

request_shape.input: OutputRequest(destination, content, labels, clearance, output_id); content must pass output_data.validate_output_request (finite JSON-like data, bounded depth and budget)
request_shape.output: the identical request.content when labels.confidentiality is a subset of clearance

operations.policy_hook: HostRouter.route -> policy.object_permission(principal, OutputRequest); ESCALATE withholds the output as OutputApprovalRequired
operations.effect: Returns the authorized content to the mediated publication API; nothing else is written

proof.note: That every framework publication API routes through OutputMediator is a regression-backed premise (SGV109/SGV110).

operations.purpose: Hook point before an LLM call made through the runtime's model operation (D9).
operations.trust_note: Only the capability decision is enforced; the allowlisted model client runs in the trusted controller. Under D11 trusted application code may also call the LLM directly, as pandas does inside its node functions; those calls are not policed by this hook.

request_shape.input: ModelInvocationRequest(model, context: tuple[LabeledValue, ...], invocation_id) built from MODEL_READ state reads
request_shape.output: the authorized context tuple; the model call itself is made by the admitted MODEL_CALL node only after allow

operations.policy_hook: HostRouter.route -> policy.object_permission(principal, ModelInvocationRequest); deny means the LLM is never invoked
operations.effect: None by the runtime; on allow the admitted MODEL_CALL node (exact allowlisted chat-model class) performs the provider call

proof.note: Proves the hook placement and router return protocol, not model content.

operations.pandas_note: Pandas calls ChatOpenAI directly inside trusted node functions (D11); routing those calls through the hook is a deployer choice.

operations.purpose: Dispatch a model-requested call to an untrusted tool implementation through an exact ToolNode and HostRouter.
operations.trust_note: Tool bodies are untrusted (D11) and run in the language sandbox or an isolated host executor.

request_shape.input: one ToolCall to an admitted tool name with JSON arguments

operations.policy_hook: HostRouter.invoke: policy tool permission; admission.recheck re-reads the captured executor/dispatcher/authorizer identity before each dispatch
operations.effect: The admitted tool body runs under the selected executor; its result is returned as data

proof.note: language-sandbox-tool additionally names lean-audit:proofs/language-route and language-derivation; its SGV903 runtime evidence is pending in supported-surface.json.

operations.pandas_note: Pandas has no third-party tools. Its compute call reaches the worker through ToolNode([compute]) and HostRouter.invoke, which the compute route covers.

operations.purpose: Expose only profile-declared graph channels to a secured tool or mediated model node.
operations.trust_note: Runtime machinery (D11, threat model TCB); authorized by HostRouter.state but its effect is not proved.

request_shape.input: StateRequest(TOOL_READ or MODEL_READ, resource=channel, owner_id, tool_name, value)
request_shape.output: the stored value (TOOL_READ) or LabeledValue (MODEL_READ) for that principal and channel

operations.policy_hook: HostRouter.route -> policy.object_permission(principal, StateRequest); ToolObjectDac.readable_channels limits channels
operations.effect: Reads the in-memory channel value held by ObjectManagerHost

proof.note: router-source-proof fixes HostRouter.state's return protocol; ObjectManagerHost._state_operation correctness is a trusted-runtime premise.

operations.purpose: Write a mediated node's output channels through the router.
operations.trust_note: Runtime machinery (D11). Trusted application nodes write graph channels through Pregel directly and do not use this operation.
operations.effect: Stores a LabeledValue keyed by principal and channel in ObjectManagerHost

operations.purpose: Authenticated checkpoint read, write and restore through MediatedCheckpointer.
operations.trust_note: Runtime machinery (D11); checkpoints are sealed and authenticated with the configured checkpoint key.

request_shape.input: StateRequest(CHECKPOINT_READ, CHECKPOINT_WRITE or RESTORE); RESTORE carries a CheckpointEnvelope
request_shape.output: the checkpoint value, or the verified envelope payload on RESTORE

operations.effect: Passes checkpoint data to the underlying saver; RESTORE verifies the envelope digest first

operations.purpose: Release a withheld (ESCALATE) request after a bound human approval.
operations.trust_note: Runtime machinery (D11); resume reruns resume permission and the complete hook chain.

request_shape.input: the original framework request plus one Approval
request_shape.output: the authorized effect of the original request

operations.policy_hook: policy.object_resume_permission(principal, request, approval); anything but ALLOW raises
operations.effect: Dispatches the original request once to ObjectManagerHost

operations.purpose: Pinned, authorized, bounded read of a registered dataset for the computation (replaces pd.read_csv in the parent).
operations.trust_note: Performed by trusted runtime code after authorization; the bytes become inert input to compute.

request_shape.input: read_dataset(principal, dataset_id, *, registry: DatasetRegistry, authorize) or aread_dataset(...); the caller names an id only; path, sha256, max_bytes and format come from the operator DatasetEntry; policy sees DatasetReadRequest(dataset_id, principal_id)
request_shape.output: inert bytes of the pinned file, at most DatasetEntry.max_bytes, whose sha256 equals the pin

operations.policy_hook: authorize(principal, DatasetReadRequest) must return an exact Decision with Verdict.ALLOW and no constraints, before any open
operations.effect: One openat2 (no symlinks) pinned read of a registered regular file, bounded by max_bytes and checked against the pinned sha256

proof.note: Ordering derived from source (policy allow before any open, pinned no-symlink open, digest of the returned bytes) plus fixed controls; premises: kernel openat2, operator registry, trusted caller (D11).

unmapped_routes.sql-bounded-select: unsupported route of the SQL cohort; outside the pandas catalog (D10)

excluded.reason: Pandas issues no DispatchRequest; its nested agents run inside trusted application nodes (D11).
No child principal is derived by pandas.
Under closed admission a subgraph node body is not an admitted kind.
Send fan-out is not an admitted framework branch.
Nested agents run as trusted application code, not as a mediated dispatch.
Pandas registers its single compute tool statically at ToolNode construction.
Pandas configures no store, so MediatedStore is never installed.
SessionFlowPolicy.guard_operation is not used by pandas.
